vulnerability: Attackers can insert malicious code or fake entries into logs; Many IP cameras use weak passwords and outdated firmware.
controls: Use MFA + mandated strong passwords for IP cameras; Manage logs in a secured and centralized system.

vulnerability: An employee leaves their computer open while going on a bathroom break
controls: Raise awareness for this risk and tell employees to lock their computer to protect company and personal data.

vulnerability: Stress from extreme weather and increasing electricity demand.
controls: Upgrade stronger materials, bury selected critical lines in high-risk areas, and use drones and AI analysis to spot any weaknesses

vulnerability: Throwing out packages can show what the company has inside.
controls: Ensure anything thrown out has been broken down or any labels have been properly ripped off.

vulnerability: Suspicious people can slip in through usually locked doors when an employee goes through them.
controls: Replace locked doors with key scanners where a person can only access an area with an employee card. The door would close immediately after the person passes and security by the lobby can watch over the doors.

vulnerability: An employee's access badge could be cloned by attackers using skimming devices to read the radio frequency signal of the badge.
controls: Use multi-factor authentication with biometrics scanners and a unique personal identification number alongside badge scan. Moreover, the company should segment the facilities into sections with different levels of accessibility.

vulnerability: An employee may have a large monitor and a person who may have sneaked in can record or watch their screen.
controls: This could be fixed with the same method used for tailgating where they stop before they enter. If they still enter the building, there can be more employee access doors to heavily restricted spaces.

vulnerability: Dev endpoints using static API keys
controls: Require YubiKeys for all code commits and repository keys with hardware security module for cryptographic signing of build releases.
